article_title: Jellyfin Loses Project Leader and Two Longtime Members in Nine Days as Burnout and an AI-Tooling Dispute Collide
summary: Rejected: the headline, summary, and Overview lead all assert a fabricated 'nine-day' span between the three departures; the cited sources establish only a two-day gap (July 17 to July 19, 2026), and no source supports a nine-day figure.

findings.details:
forum.jellyfin.org: https://forum.jellyfin.org/t-project-leadership-changes
jellyfin.org: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/contributing/llm-policies/. Both are official, first-party Jellyfin project domains (the project's own community forum, used for Boniface's and Lavado's own resignation statements; and the project's own official documentation site, used for the LLM policy text). Content was independently verified against the snapshot and is accurate. This is a config/allowlist gap, not a source-credibility problem.

findings.message: Headline, summary, and Overview lead assert a fabricated 'nine-day' timeframe that is unsupported by and contradicted by the cited sources
findings.details: The headline ends '...in Nine Days...', the submission summary states the three departures happened '...within nine days...', and the Overview lead states '...within a nine-day span in July...'. All three instances describe the same claim: that Boniface, Lavado, and Rabert's departures spanned nine days. The cited sources establish the opposite. Rabert resigned effective 2026-07-17 (GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#609, opened 'on Jul 17, 2026', body: 'I made the decision to leave the Jellyfin organization entirely on 2026-07-17'; corroborated by Linuxiac: 'Andrew Rabert's resignation on July 17'). Boniface and Lavado's departure was effective 2026-07-19 (Jellyfin forum post 'Project Leadership Changes', posted 2026-07-20 at 03:01 PM, opening line 'Effective yesterday, Anthony and I decided to depart from the project...'; corroborated by Linuxiac: 'Boniface announced that he and Lavado will leave their roles effective July 19, 2026'). July 17 to July 19, 2026 is a two-day span, not nine. No source snapshot — Linuxiac, the Jellyfin forum thread, GitHub issue #609, issue #109, the LLM policy page, PR #1947, or the jellium-desktop repo page — contains the word 'nine' or supports any nine-day interval between these events. This is the article's central framing device, restated three times at the headline/summary/lead level, and is not a subordinate or recoverable detail.

content_preview.title: Jellyfin Loses Project Leader and Two Longtime Members in Nine Days as Burnout and an AI-Tooling Dispute Collide
content_preview.summary: Jellyfin's project leader, a core team member, and a longtime contributor left within nine days, citing burnout and friction over AI-assisted development.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Jellyfin, the open-source self-hosted media server, lost its project leader and two other longtime contributors within a nine-day span in July, in a leadership shake-up that its own departing leader described as amicable but that also surfaced an internal dispute over AI-assisted coding tools. According to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/jellyfin-loses-project-leader-and-core-team-member-in-major-shake-up/), project leader Joshua Boniface and longtime core team member Anthony Lavado...

recommendations: Do not resubmit this exact draft. If the bot re-reports this story, it must independently re-derive the timeline from the actual departure dates (July 17 Rabert; July 19 Boniface/Lavado — a two-day gap) rather than repeating a 'nine-day' framing, and should not assume a prior draft's headline arithmetic is correct.

Separately from this rejection: forum.jellyfin.org and jellyfin.org are legitimate first-party primary sources (the project's own forum and documentation) and are good candidates for config/source_allowlist.txt in a future batch update.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Why It Matters), 855 words (within the News 400-1200 range), appropriately hedged language ('argued', 'according to', 'raises questions about'), no AI self-reference, no sensationalism in the prose itself. Aside from the headline-level date error below, this is a well-sourced, carefully attributed piece of reporting.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 7 cited sources were fetched successfully (HTTP 200) by chief:review and saved as gzipped HTML snapshots under sources/2026-07/jellyfin-loses-project-leader-and-two-longtime-members-in-nine-days-as-burnout-and-an-ai-tooling-dispute-collide/. I verified the sha256 of all 7 snapshot files against manifest.json (all match) and personally read the extracted text of every snapshot (no live WebFetch was used; no snapshot failed). Findings per source: (1) source-0.html.gz / linuxiac.com — confirms the Boniface/Lavado July 19 effective date, Boniface's burnout quote verbatim, Boniface's Jellyfin-since-2018/Emby-fork background, Lavado's administrative role and the 'no indication...being abandoned' framing, and Rabert's July 17 resignation and AI-tooling friction framing. (2) source-1.html.gz / forum.jellyfin.org thread — confirms, verbatim, every direct quote attributed to Boniface and Lavado in the article, including 'I simply could no longer provide the effort...', 'there is good communication lines, so there is little to no risk of a hostile fork...', 'Now here we are 7-and-a-half years later...probably 10x that many individual users', and Lavado's 'After 7.5 - nearly 8 - years...' and 'fully committed to a smooth transition'. Post is dated 2026-07-20 and states the departure was 'Effective yesterday' (= July 19). (3) source-2.html.gz / GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#609 — confirms, verbatim, every quote attributed to Rabert ('burnout working within the Jellyfin organization', 'the Jellyfin organization entirely', the December 2025 rewrite / HDR-and-Qt framing, 'only a handful of organization members', 'the general attitude was very negative and increasingly burdensome and restrictive', 'lost almost all motivation', 'my passion - my default hobby to relax'), and the reference to issue #109 as 'an early sign'. Issue opened Jul 17, 2026; body states the departure decision was made '2026-07-17'. (4) source-3.html.gz / GitHub issue andrewrabert/jellium-desktop#109 — confirms the exact issue title quoted in the article ('Inclusion of CLAUDE.md violates Jellyfin LLM policy against inclusion of LLM metafiles') and that it was opened Apr 5, 2026 (matches article's 'filed... in April'). Note for context (not in the article, and not a factual error, but worth recording): the issue is marked 'Closed as not planned'. (5) source-4.html.gz / jellyfin.org LLM policy page — confirms both quotes attributed to it verbatim: 'do not commit LLM metafiles (e.g. .claude configs) or any other editor-created non-code files' and 'seeing a precipitous rise in contributors using AI within the Jellyfin ecosystem, both in the server and for clients, as well as a rise in criticism and concern about LLMs generally'. (6) source-5.html.gz / GitHub PR jellyfin/jellyfin.org#1947 — confirms the exact PR title ('Remove Joshua Boniface and Anthony Lavado'), that it was opened by joshuaboniface and merged into master on Jul 20, 2026. (7) source-6.html.gz / jellium-desktop GitHub repo — confirms the repo's own description, 'An unofficial desktop client for Jellyfin', quoted verbatim in the article, and a star count of '1.5k' (article rounds this to 'more than 1,500', a minor imprecision since 1.5k could denote anywhere from roughly 1,450 up — not material enough to be a standalone finding). CRITICAL: none of the 7 snapshots contains the word 'nine' or supports a nine-day interval between any of the reported events; cross-referencing the dates each snapshot does report (July 17 Rabert, July 19 Boniface/Lavado, July 20 forum post and PR merge, July 21 Linuxiac publication) shows a maximum four-day spread across all reported events and a two-day gap between the two departure events the headline is built around.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every direct quote in the article was checked word-for-word against its source snapshot and is verbatim and accurately attributed — no hallucinated quotes were found anywhere in this piece, which is unusual in a good way for an article of this length. However, the headline/summary/lead 'nine-day' framing is a fabricated or grossly miscalculated specific: the sources place the first and last reported departures two days apart (July 17 and July 19, 2026), not nine. See the Factual Accuracy finding above for full detail.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and carefully hedged. The article correctly keeps Boniface/Lavado's stated reason (burnout) analytically separate from Rabert's (AI-tooling friction) rather than conflating them into a single cause, uses 'argued' rather than a flatter verb when describing issue #109's characterization of the LLM policy, and balances the 'Why It Matters' section with both the departing leaders' own reassurances and the countervailing fact that three long-tenured contributors left in a short window. No loaded language or uncritical adoption of either side's framing was found. This assessment reflects the heightened scrutiny warranted by a personnel/governance dispute involving named individuals.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ (all months) and the rest of src/content/ for any prior Jellyfin coverage; found none. This is a genuinely new topic for the archive, not a duplicate.
concerns: The headline ('...in Nine Days...'), the submission summary ('left within nine days'), and the Overview lead ('within a nine-day span in July') all state a nine-day timeframe for the three departures. Per the cited sources, the actual gap between Rabert's July 17 resignation and Boniface/Lavado's July 19 effective departure is two days. No cited source supports a nine-day figure. Because this fabricated number is the headline's central framing device (not a subordinate body claim), a corrections note cannot honestly cover it without contradicting the headline the reader saw first — this is a REJECT-level issue per editorial policy, not an APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS-level one.

Minor, non-blocking: the article rounds the jellium-desktop repo's '1.5k' GitHub star count to 'more than 1,500'; a strictly accurate reading of GitHub's rounded display would be 'about 1,500'. Not material and not a reason for concern on its own.

Minor, non-blocking: forum.jellyfin.org and jellyfin.org are not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt, producing an automated warning. Both were independently verified as legitimate first-party primary sources; this is a config gap, not a sourcing problem.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. This is otherwise a strongly-sourced, quote-verified, neutrally-toned article — all 7 sources were read in full and every direct quote checked out verbatim — but the headline, summary, and lead all rest on a 'nine-day' timeframe for the three departures that the article's own cited sources contradict (the actual gap is two days, July 17 to July 19, 2026). Per editorial policy, a fabricated or unsourced fact that the headline/summary/lead depends on is a REJECT, not a corrections candidate, because the correction would have to contradict the headline itself. The contributor bot does not get a rewrite pass on this submission under v3.9.0; if the story is still worth covering, it should be resubmitted as a new submission with an accurate timeline.
